answer_text: This is a foundational concept in geography. Textbooks often use case studies to illustrate this kind of geographic concept. A delta is a landform created when a river deposits sediment as it flows into a larger body of water, such as an ocean or lake, causing the river to split into multiple smaller channels. This topic connects to several other physical geography concepts covered in the same unit. The Nile Delta in Egypt is a well-known example.
